subject: Decision Making
title: What Is a Nudge
description: A quick, practical guide to What Is a Nudge.

hook.text: A fly etched into a urinal reduced spillage by 80%. Nobody was forced. Nobody was told. Just a tiny design change.

buildup.text: Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein defined a nudge as any change in choice architecture that alters behavior predictably.

discovery.text: A nudge does not ban options or change economic incentives. It preserves freedom while guiding better choices.

twist.text: The cafeteria that puts fruit at eye level and cake in the back is nudging. You can still get cake. Most grab fruit.

climax.text: Nudges work because humans rely on mental shortcuts. Good design channels those shortcuts toward better outcomes.

punchline.text: A fly in a urinal changed behavior. No rules, no force, just design.

quiz.question: What defines a nudge?
options: A change in choice architecture that guides behavior while preserving freedom
